data.body: LLM-Review ps1 = PASS (+1) with 3 ADVISORY findings; dispositions: (1) batch_dispatch delete_one mutation['key'] vs .get('key'): ACCEPTED as-is. Reverting to .get('key') fails mypy (delete_issue expects str, .get returns Any|None); the old .get passed only via the removed _call_with_retry wrapper's loose typing. A delete batch dict always carries 'key' (built in apply_handlers), so ['key'] is the type-correct fail-fast form; passing None to delete_issue would be the real bug. (2) census AC4 static source-text absence check and (3) AC6 docstring-prose grep flagged as change-detectors: these are the AC4/AC6-MANDATED source-absence + rollback-guidance proofs, complemented by the file's runtime poison tests. Strengthening AC6 into a behavioral 'rollback never calls delete_issue' assertion is deferred to T3 (a735), whose file_impact finalizes this census with full E2E.
